summary.headline: Go Fashion Q2 FY27 revenue fell 3% YoY to Rs 218 crore; gross margin 60.8% and SSSG roughly flat amid festive shift and RM inflation.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue declined 3% YoY to Rs 218 crore as the festive season shifted into October, with LFS dispatches moving out of September. Gross margin fell to 60.8% as higher-cost fabric inventory flowed through; management estimates a 200 bps hit in Q2 and 100-200 bps again in Q3. EBITDA before exceptionals was Rs 56 crore (25.8% margin) and PAT was Rs 9 crore. Store network consolidation continued: 23 closures and 9 openings in Q2, taking the EBO count to 737 with total retail area up to about 4.4 lakh sq ft. Management guided to lower closures and price hikes from post-festive, but gave no formal guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Q2 impact of about 200 bps from RM inflation (management estimate)
Store-closure capex write-offs; H1 FY26 was Rs 1.73 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Operating cash flow pre-Ind AS 116 (H1 FY27)

segments.name: EBO (company-operated stores)
segments.commentary: Same-store sales growth broadly flat in Q2 after +0.6% in Q1; 737 EBOs across 196 cities. Stores above 750 sq ft reportedly at +2-3% SSSG while smaller stores are negative; average EBO size about 608 sq ft.

segments.name: LFS (large format stores)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue hit by festive timing, with dispatches moved from September to October. LFS was about 23% of H1 FY27 sales; management says supply chain is normalised.

segments.name: Dailywear concept
segments.commentary: 21 operational stores vs 15 in Q1, with a target of 25-30 by end FY27 (8-9 more planned). Management cites about Rs 1,000 sales per sq ft per month as a benchmark.

segments.name: Online / quick commerce / Amazon
segments.commentary: Online receivables rose after quick commerce and Amazon SOR tie-ups began from March; receivables rose from Rs 106 crore to Rs 125 crore.

guidance_outlook: SSSG target: positive for FY27 as a whole; management says it is 'keeping fingers crossed' and Q3 'should deliver a good number'.
Gross margin: 100-200 bps impact expected in Q3 FY27; margins expected to stabilise over the next 2 quarters as calibrated price hikes offset RM costs.
Store closures: Q3 closures visibility at 15-20 stores, sharply lower than Q1 (58-59) and Q2 (23); management says closures will 'considerably' decline in H2.
Dailywear: target of 25-30 stores by end FY27.
Inventory days to remain within the 90-100 day range guided earlier in the year.
Long term: about 2x square footage over the next 5 years, COCO model retained; bottomwear stores to move to 700-900 sq ft.
capex_capacity: Retail area about 4.4 lakh sq ft at 30 Sep 2026, up from 4.34 lakh at 31 Mar 2026 (about 14,220 sq ft added in H1 despite net closures).
H1 FY27 openings 24 and closures 89; Q2 openings 9 and closures 23.
Store renovations undertaken in H1 (a couple of stores), included in other expenses; value not disclosed.
Men's and women's topwear pilot: 21 stores above 1,500 sq ft; plan to add 8-9 more to test the topwear format.
demand_pricing: Festive timing shifted; management says a portion of pre-festive demand moved from September to October. Festive season started decently; 49 days to festive used as the leading indicator.
Price hikes taken on certain articles recently, with more planned post-festive; ASP for EBOs Rs 827 (H1). Management says ASP rise of 6% is mainly product mix, not price.
Fabric/yarn costs up 8-10% blended, after the geopolitical situation; management had expected cooling in Jul-Aug but prices stayed high.
Full-price sales ratio 93% in H1 FY27.
Value-added non-leggings portfolio now 70% of revenue; new bottomwear products in the Rs 800-900 price band.
Shraddha Kapoor brand campaign went live in Q2 (ambassador from July); effect to be assessed after the festive season.

qa_highlights.question: Why have costs not fallen after closing about 75 net stores YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost was flat at about Rs 46.3 crore in Q2 vs Rs 45.75 crore a year ago, after April increments. Rent was about Rs 37 crore vs Rs 36 crore. Advertising rose to Rs 12.63 crore in H1 from Rs 7.85 crore, and exceptional write-offs rose to Rs 9.87 crore from Rs 1.73 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company taking price hikes to offset cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Some hikes have been taken and more are planned post-festive. Management expects margin offset to take a couple of quarters, with stabilisation in the next 2 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will closures slow down, and will H2 be better than H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said closures will be considerably lower from Q3 (15-20 stores visible), and Q3 should deliver a good YoY number. On whether FY27 SSSG turns positive, management said it was 'keeping fingers crossed'.

qa_highlights.question: How much new-cost inventory is flowing through, given the inventory and COGS figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is hard to isolate because products sell at different rates and price hikes are happening. It estimated a 200 bps GM hit in Q2 and 100-200 bps in Q3, and acknowledged older inventory at old prices.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables rose from Rs 106 crore to Rs 125 crore despite lower LFS revenue; why?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase is mainly non-LFS: online receivables from quick commerce and Amazon SOR since March, plus some export receivables for the Dubai store.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the LFS discount jumped to Rs 61 crore in FY26 from Rs 44.5 crore in FY25?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LFS credits are margin-linked (about 5-6% of LFS sales, reconciled in Q4) rather than discounts. It did not confirm the Rs 61 crore figure and promised a clarification note; FY26 LFS decline was due to Q3 supply chain disruption at a large partner.

risks_watch: Gross margin: management expects 100-200 bps pressure in Q3 and says the 200 bps Q2 hit is not a precise figure; the timing of price-hike pass-through is uncertain.

SSSG: Q2 was flat with a festive shift; Q3 needs to be strong for FY27 SSSG to turn positive. Smaller stores (<300 sq ft, roughly 120-150 units) remain negative and 20-30% of the network is seen as problematic.
Competition and store format: management attributes slowdown to store size, not merchandise or competition (Zudio, Westside), but this is not independently verified.
Clarifications pending: store-count split by size (to be shared via SGA), LFS discount quantum (Rs 61 crore vs Rs 44.5 crore), and receivables rise from Rs 106 crore to Rs 125 crore.
Topwear and menswear pilot (21 stores) is unproven; a 8-9 store test is still to come.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term store-format transition and the early signals, but cautious and at times evasive on specific numbers (store-size breakup, SSSG timing, margin quantum, LFS discount), promising follow-up data via SGA.
key_quotes: As I said last quarter, one quarter does not make a trend in either direction.
So, if you ask me, the store is the real reason for our slowness. And I think the larger store is what is going to fix it.
This is a shift in timing rather than demand and the supply chain with the key LFS partners remains normalized.

growth.why: No formal revenue guidance; management says FY27 SSSG should be positive but 'keeping fingers crossed', with Dailywear targeted at 25-30 stores by FY27-end (from 21), Q3 closures falling to 15-20, and a 100-200 bps gross margin hit in Q3, while Q2 revenue fell 3% YoY and H1 was down 1.5%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin fell to 60.8% in Q2 (about 200 bps RM hit) and management expects a further 100-200 bps hit in Q3, with stabilisation only in the next 2 quarters as price hikes offset fabric costs up 8-10%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Dailywear stores at 21 vs 15 in Q1, with a firm target of 25-30 by FY27-end (8-9 more), plus an 8-9 store topwear pilot; retail area only ~4.4 lakh sq ft, so these are small adds against 89 closures in H1.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 revenue fell 3% YoY to Rs 218 crore and H1 fell 1.5% to Rs 440 crore, with SSSG flat in Q2; management hopes Q3 'should deliver a good number' but FY27 SSSG positivity is only 'fingers crossed'.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed beyond store renovations (value undisclosed) and the long-term plan of about 2x square footage over 5 years.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No formal guidance was given, and management is only 'keeping fingers crossed' on positive FY27 SSSG with H1 revenue down 1.5% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 gross margin hit of 100-200 bps is guided, price-hike pass-through timing is uncertain, and smaller stores (20-30% of network) remain problematic with negative SSSG.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New bottomwear products in the Rs 800-900 price band are already in place, and the topwear format is being tested in 21 stores with 8-9 more planned; value-added non-leggings are 70% of revenue.

rows.label: Store closures slow sharply in H2
rows.why: Q3 closure visibility is 15-20 stores vs 58-59 in Q1 and 23 in Q2, and management says closures will 'considerably' decline in H2.

rows.label: Post-festive price hikes
rows.why: Some hikes are taken, more are planned post-festive, and management expects margin offset over a couple of quarters; fabric costs are up 8-10%.

rows.label: Quick commerce and Amazon SOR channel
rows.why: Online receivables rose from Rs 106 crore to Rs 125 crore after the quick commerce and Amazon SOR tie-ups began in March, showing channel traction.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term store-format shift, Dailywear and the lower Q3 closure count, but cautious and at times evasive on SSSG timing, the margin quantum and the LFS discount, promising follow-up data via SGA; analysts pushed on margin, store-size breakup, receivables and the LFS
